name: Solomon at Gibeon
charge: Asking for an understanding heart to judge the people, and not for long life, riches, or the life of his enemies
summary: Offered anything he wanted, the young king asked for wisdom to judge a great people. The speech pleased the Lord, who gave him the wisdom and added the riches and honour he had not asked. The kingdom he built on it was the greatest Israel ever had. What he did with his wives afterward is another case.
offense: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people? And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing. In Wisdom: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me; I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
judgment: Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment; behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee. And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour. All the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.

entries.commentary: Solomon makes affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt and takes his daughter, while building his own house, the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem. He loves the Lord and walks in the statutes of David his father, though the people still sacrifice in high places because no house was yet built to the name of the Lord.

At Gibeon the Most High appears to Solomon in a dream and says, ask what I shall give thee. Solomon, calling himself a little child who knows not how to go out or come in, asks for an understanding heart to judge the great people, to discern between good and bad. This is what we still need to pray for. We should pray that the Most High endows our leadership with wisdom, and that we ourselves learn wisdom in these scriptures and how to judge matters among one another. -

Because Solomon asked for understanding to discern judgment and not for long life, riches, or the life of his enemies, the Most High gives him a wise and understanding heart like no other before or after. He also gives what Solomon did not ask, riches and honor, and promises length of days if he walks in his ways.

Two harlots come before the king, each claiming the living child, after one woman's child died in the night and she exchanged it. Solomon calls for a sword and commands the living child divided in two, and gives half to each. The true mother pleads that the child be given alive to the other rather than slain, and by this the king discerns her, for her bowels yearned upon her son. All Israel hears the judgment and fears the king, for they see the wisdom of God is in him to do judgment.

Solomon is king over all Israel, and these are the princes he set: priests, scribes, a recorder, one over the host, one over the officers, one over the household, and one over the tribute. Twelve officers provide victuals for the king and his household, each man his month in the year. This is the establishment of government, showing order. There is the king, then ranking men, each with a position of order, the same pattern of captains and officers set up in the days of Moses.

Judah and Israel are as many as the sand by the sea, eating, drinking, and making merry, and Solomon reigns over all the kingdoms from the river to the border of Egypt, who bring presents and serve him. Every man dwells safely under his vine and fig tree from Dan to Beersheba. Israel dwells safely because of the wars of King David, who put down all the surrounding nations and put them to tribute. That is why Solomon is able to rule in a time of peace.

The Most High gives Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, largeness of heart as the sand on the seashore, so that his wisdom excels all the children of the east country and all the wisdom of Egypt. He is wiser than all men, speaks three thousand proverbs, and his songs are a thousand and five, which is why we have Proverbs and the Song of Songs. He speaks of trees, beasts, fowl, creeping things, and fishes, and people of all nations come to hear his wisdom. Since his wisdom already excelled Egypt's, we have no need to dabble in Egyptology or any doctrine outside the scriptures given to us. -

When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Most High, she came to prove him with hard questions, and came to Jerusalem with a great train, camels bearing spices, much gold, and precious stones. She communed with him of all that was in her heart, and Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hid from the king that he told her not.

When the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon's wisdom, the house he built, the meat of his table, the sitting of his servants, their apparel, his cupbearers, and his ascent to the house of the Most High, there was no more spirit in her. Everything in the kingdom was in order, the servants in uniform, the cupbearers in place; this is why order matters in the body today, so that those who come in are astonished and the worldly spirit of disorder leaves them, seeing the discipline and love for the people.

She told the king the report she heard in her own land was true, that she had not believed it until her eyes had seen it, and behold the half was not told her; his wisdom and prosperity exceeded the fame she heard. She said happy are his men and servants that stand continually before him and hear his wisdom; they were happy to be in order, serving with joyfulness and not complaining, because Solomon ruled wisely and took care of his people. She blessed the Most High who delighted in Solomon to set him on the throne of Israel, because the Most High loved Israel forever; even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people.

She gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in great store, and precious stones; and the navy of Hiram brought from Ophir great plenty of almug trees and precious stones, of which Solomon made pillars for the house of the Most High and harps and psalteries for singers. Solomon knew how to entertain the people, providing for singing and joyfulness in the house of the Most High, for he had vision for the house and wanted Israel to enjoy the feasts and serve with gladness of heart. Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked. People assume this was sexual, but her desire was to know his wisdom and see his order; the word desire in scripture does not always mean what people think, as the law shows the tithe money could be spent on whatever the soul lusted after, meaning oxen, sheep, wine, and food. Nothing is said of her being pregnant. The Ethiopian tradition claims Solomon fathered a son with her and founded a dynasty, but the scripture gives no such thing; she turned and went to her own country with her servants.

The weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents, besides that of the merchants and the kings of Arabia and the governors. He made two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold, and a great throne of ivory overlaid with the best gold. The throne had six steps, a round top, stays on either side, and two lions by the stays with twelve lions on the six steps, such as was not made in any kingdom. These standing lions were not graven images to bow down to; the law forbids images set up to worship, but these were not worshipped. All Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were pure gold; silver was nothing accounted of in his days. Once in three years the navy of Tarshish brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and wisdom, and all the earth sought him to hear the wisdom the Most High put in his heart, bringing presents year by year. No king reigned like Solomon or was richer than him. He gathered a thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, placed in the cities and at Jerusalem; these were of his own people, so he provided jobs for them rather than making them slaves. He made silver in Jerusalem as stones, and had horses and linen yarn brought out of Egypt; a chariot came up for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Solomon bought the best of everything, but there comes a point where riches and power can pervert the mind if a man is not grounded, and that is what begins to happen.

Solomon the son of David was strengthened in his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and magnified him exceedingly. The Most High established Solomon before he ever built the house. Solomon spake to all Israel, to the captains of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges and to every governor, the chief of the fathers, and went with all the congregation to the high place at Gibeon, where the tabernacle of the congregation that Moses had made in the wilderness was. The ark of God had already been brought up by David from Kirjathjearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem. To read that history, go back to Second Samuel 6, and to First Chronicles 15.

The brasen altar that Bezaleel the son of Uri had made was set before the tabernacle of the Lord, and Solomon and the congregation sought unto it. Solomon went up to that brasen altar before the Lord and offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it. In that night the Most High appeared unto Solomon and said, Ask what I shall give thee. This same account is told in First Kings chapter 3, where the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night; reading it there gives more detail of what was said. Solomon answered that the Lord had shewed great mercy unto David his father and made him to reign in his stead, and asked that the promise unto David be established, for the Lord had made him king over a people like the dust of the earth in multitude. Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge that he might go out and come in before the people, for who could judge so great a people. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.

The Most High said to Solomon that because this was in his heart, and he had not asked riches, wealth, honor, the life of his enemies, nor long life, but wisdom and knowledge to judge the people, wisdom and knowledge were granted unto him. The Lord also gave Solomon riches, wealth, and honor such as no king before him had, and none after him would have the like. When a man seeks the things of the Most High first, the other things are added unto him. Solomon returned from the high place at Gibeon to Jerusalem and reigned over Israel. He gathered chariots and horsemen, having a thousand and four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, which he placed in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem. The king made silver and gold at Jerusalem as plenteous as stones, and cedars as the sycomore trees in the valley for abundance. Horses were brought out of Egypt, and the merchants received the linen yarn at a price and fetched up horses and chariots for all the kings of the Hittites and of Syria.

verses.text: In Gibeon the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.

And Solomon said, Thou hast shewed unto thy servant David my father great mercy, according as he walked before thee in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with thee; and thou hast kept for him this great kindness, that thou hast given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.
And now, O Lord my God, thou hast made thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in.
And thy servant is in the midst of thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.
Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?
And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.

And God said unto him, Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment;
Behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.
And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour: so that there shall not be any among the kings like unto thee all thy days.
And if thou wilt walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as thy father David did walk, then I will lengthen thy days.
And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore.
And Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.
For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.
And he spake three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five.
And he spake of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall: he spake also of beasts, and of fowl, and of creeping things, and of fishes.
And there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, which had heard of his wisdom.
So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom.
And all the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
In that night did God appear unto Solomon, and said unto him, Ask what I shall give thee.
And Solomon said unto God, Thou hast shewed great mercy unto David my father, and hast made me to reign in his stead.
Now, O Lord God, let thy promise unto David my father be established: for thou hast made me king over a people like the dust of the earth in multitude.
Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who can judge this thy people, that is so great?

And God said to Solomon, Because this was in thine heart, and thou hast not asked riches, wealth, or honour, nor the life of thine enemies, neither yet hast asked long life; but hast asked wisdom and knowledge for thyself, that thou mayest judge my people, over whom I have made thee king:

Wisdom and knowledge is granted unto thee; and I will give thee riches, and wealth, and honour, such as none of the kings have had that have been before thee, neither shall there any after thee have the like.
Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
Neither compared I unto her any precious stone, because all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.
I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.
All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands.
And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goeth before them: and I knew not that she was the mother of them.
I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.
For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.
If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
